chapter: The war years: Barnet, Hot Lips Page, Newton and Kirby
title: Charlie Barnet as a boss; leaving and joining Kirby
summary: Barnet was great but often absent; he advised Ramirez not to be broke; Ralph Burns replaced Ramirez and he later joined John Kirby.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: How did you find Charlie as a boss?
He was great. Charlie was beautiful. He was a fine fellow. But he didn't stay with the band much. I think Charlie had other problems, I guess, bringing a vocalist here, a vocalist there...
Well, he was marrying a new one every year about that time?

Well, Charlie would... Sometimes he'd pick up something in his mail, he had loaned somebody some money and the guy opened up a business and all of sudden he's half-owner or something like that! I guess money brings money.
But Charlie used to say to me, "Man, whatever you do, try not to be broke." [LAUGHS] I remember he said, "It makes all the difference in the world." I'll never forget that.

Now, it was early in the game. Then when he came back... We agreed to disagree, somehow or other. Ralph Burns replaced me in the band. They picked him up... I wanted to come back to New York, and they picked him up in Wisconsin. We made tours all over, you know, Wisconsin, Chicago, Omaha, Des Moines, Iowa... We played the Apollo.
Of course, he used to play the Apollo every year, didn't he.
Yeah, we played the Apollo. Later on, after him, I joined Kirby, John Kirby.
